Sarah tries to know the 250 or so people pushing the frontier of AI research.

I asked her what's changed in how that group is thinking in the last 6 months:

"I don't think every researcher doing frontier work at these labs feels like they're essential to the machine.

With recursive self-improvement of AI research models that can improve the models themselves, we are a 1-2 years away from some sort of exponential intelligence.

That belief is new within the last 12 months for a lot of researchers.

There is some sense of the major labs are so compute-intensive and so large from a headcount perspective now that the sense of contribution, of "I can move the needle."

If OpenAI has 200 people, there's not that many researchers. The question of how do we get there is really up to every single person.

Now if the question is, well, I need $750 billion of compute spend, I think people feel less ownership of the outcome.

I definitely think there's a large contingent of researchers who would feel that one of two things is now true.

What I do doesn't matter anyway because the model is gonna do it. Or, the only thing that matters is compute scale.

And both of those are somewhat disempowering."

Adam --

Think of bitcoin as a service.  The service it provides is the ability to store wealth in a digital format without a government or a bank.

We are all used to services having value. For instance: Microsoft offers a service; the ability to edit Word and Excel documents, access cloud compute, etc.  The more people who want that service, the more valuable Microsoft is; the fewer people who want it, the less value Microsoft is; if no one wanted it, the value would be zero.

The same is true of bitcoin. 

The difference is, Microsoft is a company. To access its service, you can pay a fee to Redmond. Those fees are aggregated and paid out in dividends.

Bitcoin is not a company. The only way to access its service is to buy the asset. If you buy the asset, you get the service.

Your (eminently reasonable) criticism is that you don't like the service bitcoin provides.  But millions of people do.

I think if you frame it as a "service" you can get close to the debate of its future value.  Will more or fewer people want a digital way to store wealth that doesn't rely on a government or a bank in the future. I suspect the answer is more, but we will see!

Before you read this on how I recommend hedging your portfolio in the current environment, first read my previous tweet below it: “What Are You Hedging Against?”

The idea is simple. If your kid rides his bike only inside the house, you probably don’t need to insure it against a total loss. That would be expensive and unnecessary. You insure against the kind of damage that is actually likely to happen.

Same with hedging. First define what you are protecting against. Then build the hedge around that risk.

If everyone is already afraid of a 10% correction and hedge funds have already deleveraged, I struggle to see where the sellers come from for a full 10% drawdown.

But let’s assume they are partially right and we get a correction.

I see four possible outcomes over the next 45 days, into the October 16 expiration:

5% chance: market goes up 5% in the next 45 days

30% chance: The market goes higher. You deleveraged, so you barely participate.

30% chance: The market stays around current levels. Some stocks do well, but because you deleveraged, you probably don’t.

30% chance: We follow the historical pattern and the market corrects, but because everyone is already positioned for it, the drawdown is more like 1% to 7%, not 10%.

5% chance: The market actually falls 10% or more.

Taking that distribution into account, I like a creative hedge/trade on $QQQ into the October 16 expiration:

Buy the 715 put.
Sell 3 puts around 650, roughly 9% lower.
Sell the 750 call, roughly 5% higher.
It’s opened for a $19 credit.

The trade does especially well if the market falls somewhere between roughly 5% and 11%.

The idea is simple: stay exposed to some upside while protecting yourself against the kind of downside I think is actually more likely over the next 45 days.
